affected_system: pedestrian right-of-way, crossings, sidewalks, and accessible routes
alternatives: advance high-risk work within verified feasible windows for pedestrian right-of-way inspection and repair schedule
use rolling risk and capacity updates to reschedule pedestrian right-of-way inspection and repair schedule
pair dependency-aware work-window scheduling with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Crash, conflict, barrier, sidewalk, crossing, and demand data have explicit observation processes.
Accessibility is evaluated across route continuity, slope, surface, crossing, and obstruction dimensions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue the fixed operating calendar for pedestrian right-of-way inspection and repair schedule.

constraints.description: The pedestrian safety and universal accessibility schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: vision-zero director and accessibility compliance officer
decision_question: When should inspections and repairs occur to minimize access disruption and coordinate dependencies?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The pedestrian safety and universal accessibility schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
independence_key.decision_object: pedestrian right-of-way inspection and repair schedule
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for pedestrian right-of-way inspection and repair schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.

intended_claim: A versioned schedule design for comparing declared alternatives affecting pedestrian right-of-way inspection and repair schedule, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: distributional gap in high-consequence barrier-days awaiting verified completion
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer repair completion from work-order closure alone.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for pedestrian right-of-way inspection and repair schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.

title: Schedule sidewalk, crossing, and signal work
transportability_risks: Street design, enforcement, mobility-device needs, exposure, and reporting vary by place.
Crash-only models underrepresent near misses and unreported accessibility barriers.
